stage: development algorithm comparison, not independent population validation
algorithm: Quadratic plus offsets across gaps >0.5 d, without flux clipping.
Original and detrended top 3 LS peaks plus original/detrended BLS winners; test half, original and double within 0.05–8 d.
Two rounds of local frequency refinement using full-data phase templates.
96-bin periodic interpolation; alternate cycles train/predict each other. Gain >=20%, both folds >=10%, coverage >=80%, at least 3 cycles. These scores are not calibrated false-alarm probabilities.
Prefer the smallest half/original/double alias within 2 percentage points of best predictive gain; retain nonharmonic competitors.
Narrow dip without clear secondary, or unresolved half-cycle difference, retains orbital ambiguity.
Require all observed epochs to detect and agree within 1%; no silent dropping of a failed epoch.
Auxiliary periodic correlation |r|>=0.8 and predictive gain >=20%, or SAP disagreement, causes source-review status. Correlation is not proof of instrumental origin.
Existing pixel localization checks supplied TPF data and known neighbors. No new catalog lookup is required for offline decisions.
metrics: preferred cycle accuracy (1%); abstentions stay in the denominator
photometric P/2 recovery of equal eclipses separately from orbital ambiguity
source cautions, confirmed-variable count always zero
per-case old/new outcomes, all errors and unavailable inputs
limitations: Development thresholds are motivated by observed v1 failures and software fixtures, not learned from an untouched test sample.
Both candidate search and refinement reuse the cross-cycle data; no frequentist significance claim.
No independently labeled quiet real-star negatives yet; population false-positive rate unavailable.
Results and input hashes from v1 must remain unchanged.
